payload.text:
I'd hold the merge until one bug is fixed. The new ranking code puts the wrong player first once scores get big enough, which the README says they will.

**Blocker: `src/rank.js` sorts with `b.score - a.score`**
Scores are decimal strings because they can go past 2^53. Subtracting them turns them into ordinary JavaScript numbers, which round off past that size. The README specifically says never to do this. I tested it: with scores `9007199254740993` (player a) and `9007199254740992` (player b), passing b first gives **b rank 1, a rank 2**, which is wrong. The two values round to the same number, so the result just depends on input order.
`src/score.js` already has the right tool: `compareScore`, which handles arbitrary length. The fix is `.sort((a, b) => compareScore(b.score, a.score))`. `topN` uses `rankings`, so it gets fixed too. The test only uses small scores (5, 12, 9), which is why it passes. It needs a case above 2^53.

**Smaller things, worth fixing but not blocking:**
- **`displayName` crashes when a player has no name.** `player.name.trim()` throws if `name` is missing or null, and I confirmed it. If that can happen, `(player.name ?? '').trim()` handles it.
- **Tied scores get different ranks.** Equal scores get consecutive numbers, and their order depends on input order. If ties should share a rank (1, 1, 3), that needs handling. If not, the README should say so.
- **`topN` doesn't check `n`.** A negative `n` cuts entries off the end of the list instead of returning nothing. That's only a problem if `n` comes from user input.

The version bump, changelog and README updates look fine. As you asked, I didn't change any code.
